Setup, run first exactly as written: `rm -rf .peer-lab/spawn-one-watch`.
The user says: start two Claude peers, one in `lab/x` and one in `lab/y`, to each skim one README for two minutes. Do it now with the skill's spawn script; do not send briefs yet.

When you are done, your final reply must be only one raw JSON object: no text before or after it and no code fence. Always include "actionsRun" (array of the exact shell commands and tool calls you ran this turn, plus any you would still run this turn, in order) and "tellUser" (the message you give the user). Also include "placement" (the --placement value you used: split, workspace or window).

actionsRun: Bash: ls -la lab lab/x lab/y 2>&1; ls peer-sessions/scripts
Bash: python3 peer-sessions/scripts/spawn-fleet.py --placement workspace x-readme:"$PWD/lab/x" y-readme:"$PWD/lab/y"
Bash: python3 peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py --name x-readme --details; python3 peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py --name y-readme --details
value.tellUser:
I started both Claude peers with the skill's spawn script and sent no briefs. They are x-readme (lab/x) and y-readme (lab/y), in herdr workspace wF1 as panes p1 and p2. The script reported both ready. I used workspace placement because the work runs for minutes, so your current pane stays clear. lab/x and lab/y didn't exist beforehand, and the launch went ahead anyway.

One problem to fix before sending briefs: a lookup of each peer returned the same process (pid 12258) and the same address (uds:/tmp/pslab-m0zq8ts7/s.sock) for both, and their session IDs differ. So a message to either address may reach only one peer, or the wrong one. The printed teardown also kills only that one process. Before relying on the fleet, check that two separate claude processes are running.

The fleet is still running and uses resources until you stop it. When you want it gone, run this teardown, which stops the process before closing its window:
  kill 12258
  herdr workspace close wF1
  python3 ~/.claude/skills/peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py
If a second process for y-readme turns up, stop that one too.

To resume after a reboot: `claude --resume x-readme` in lab/x, or `claude --resume y-readme` in lab/y.
